name: Aquarium
label: Dischord
lede: A keyboard, a drum kit and a projector full of old science-class films: five years of DC shows, one tour, one album, and a two-song goodbye that arrived three years after they'd stopped.

eras.title: Songs for the classroom projector
eras.text: A duo playing instrumentals in front of vintage film reels was not what anyone expected from Dischord in the 2000s. Aquarium started as a soundtrack to science films and nature footage, then found their voice, literally, and a dedicated DC following, though Dischord says they only ever played one tour.

years.cap: Aquarium: Jason Hutto and Laura Harris
years.h: [[Jason Hutto|83a6d089-39e0-4b6a-9976-9685d18078e5]] and [[Laura Harris|5ff36e5c-65da-4d74-8929-a243430d36bc]] form Aquarium around a film projector
years.p: Keyboardist Jason Hutto, formerly of Motor-Cycle Wars, and drummer Laura Harris start Aquarium. Dischord's bio says they played atmospheric instrumentals in front of vintage film reels: science classroom fare, nature footage.
years.xp:
The films did the talking at first. Jason Hutto played electric piano and keyboards, Laura Harris played drums, and there were no vocals.

Over time Hutto started singing, and the instrumentals turned into songs.

eras.title: One album, then the lights come up
eras.text: Aquarium finally made their record at Inner Ear with a pair of Dischord's steadiest hands on the desk. It came out in October, and by the end of the year the band was over.

years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear, mixed by [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] at Trixie Studios, mastered by TJ Lipple at Silver Sonya. Eleven songs, several of them pure DC: Can't Afford To Live Here, White House, Channel 9.
Aquarium break up in 2006, the same year their self-titled album comes out on Dischord. None of the sources say why.

eras.title: The afterlife of a duo
eras.text: Aquarium's records outlasted the band: a Washington Post review after the split, a final 7" three years later. Laura Harris went on to drum in Mary Timony's Ex Hex.

years.h: The Washington Post's Express reviews Aquarium after the split
years.p: The Express reviews Aquarium's self-titled album in January 2007, with the band already finished.
A two-song 7", released three years after Aquarium broke up. The last Aquarium record.

Former Aquarium drummer Laura Harris joins [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]]'s power trio with Betsy Wright, and later tours with [[Death Valley Girls|987c6ccf-d4c5-4f23-938a-c0a21782803d]], per Wikipedia.

sources.title: Washington Post Express: The Aquarium, Water Music
